Reference binary: `/opt/uiuc-agent/home/ref_lua` (`Lua 5.5.1`, `_VERSION == "Lua 5.5"`).
Everything below was derived **only** by running that binary.
Regression tests that reproduce every table in this file live in

`string` exports (for reference):
`byte char dump find format gmatch gsub len lower match pack packsize rep reverse sub unpack upper`.
The four pattern functions are `find`, `match`, `gmatch`, `gsub`.

---

## 1. Pattern items

### 1.1 Character classes `%x`

`match_class(c, cl)` switches on `tolower(cl)`; if `cl` is uppercase the result is
negated. Exactly **eleven** letters are classes: `a c d g l p s u w x z`
(plus their uppercase complements `A C D G L P S U W X Z`).
All other `%<byte>` sequences are a literal copy of that byte.

Classes use the **C locale only** (`os.setlocale("")` returns `"C"`; there is no
other locale available in this build), so they are pure ASCII byte tests:

| class | matching bytes (decimal) | count |
|---|---|---|
| `%a` | `65-90,97-122` | 52 |
| `%c` | `0-31,127` | 33 |
| `%d` | `48-57` | 10 |
| `%g` | `33-126` | 94 |
| `%l` | `97-122` | 26 |
| `%p` | `33-47,58-64,91-96,123-126` | 32 |
| `%s` | `9-13,32` | 6 |
| `%u` | `65-90` | 26 |
| `%w` | `48-57,65-90,97-122` | 62 |
| `%x` | `48-57,65-70,97-102` | 22 |
| **`%z`** | **`0`** | **1** |
| `%A` | `0-64,91-96,123-255` | 204 |
| `%C` | `32-126,128-255` | 223 |
| `%D` | `0-47,58-255` | 246 |
| `%G` | `0-32,127-255` | 162 |
| `%L` | `0-96,123-255` | 230 |
| `%P` | `0-32,48-57,65-90,97-122,127-255` | 224 |
| `%S` | `0-8,14-31,33-255` | 250 |
| `%U` | `0-64,91-255` | 230 |
| `%W` | `0-47,58-64,91-96,123-255` | 194 |
| `%X` | `0-47,58-64,71-96,103-255` | 234 |
| **`%Z`** | **`1-255`** | **255** |

> **SURPRISE / divergence from stock 5.4:** `%z` is a live class meaning
> "the zero byte" (it is *not* the literal letter `z`), and `%Z` is its
> complement (every byte except 0).  `string.find("z","%z") == nil`,
> `string.find("\0","%z") == 1,1`.

`.` matches **any** byte (all 256, including `\0` and `\n`):
`select(2, ("<all 256 bytes>"):gsub(".","")) == 256`.

### 1.2 `%` escapes that are not classes

* `%0` … `%9` in a *pattern* are back references (§4).
* `%b` and `%f` are the balanced-match and frontier items (§5, §6).
* Every other `%<byte>` — including `%%`, `%.`, `%(`, `%-`, `%\0`, `%\200` — is
  the literal byte. 233 of the 256 `%<byte>` forms match their own character.

### 1.3 Sets `[...]`

Parsing (`classend`): after `[`, an optional `^` is skipped, then **one
character is consumed unconditionally** (this is why a `]` in first position is
literal), then bytes are consumed until an unescaped `]`; `%` always escapes the
next byte. Running off the end of the pattern ⇒ `malformed pattern (missing ']')`.

Membership (`matchbracketclass`) walks the set left to right:

1. `%X` ⇒ class/escaped literal test.
2. else if the **next** byte is `-` **and** the byte after that is still inside
   the set ⇒ range `p .. p+2`.
3. else literal byte compare.

Consequences (all verified):

| pattern | matching bytes |
|---|---|
| `[abc]` | `97-99` |
| `[^abc]` | `0-96,100-255` |
| `[a-c]` | `97-99` |
| `[c-a]` | *(none — reversed range is empty)* |
| `[]]` | `93` |
| `[]a]` | `93,97` |
| `[^]]` | `0-92,94-255` |
| `[a]]` | *(none: set `[a]` then literal `]` — 2 chars)* |
| `[[]` | `91` |
| `[%]]` | `93` |
| `[]-a]` | `93-97` (range `]`..`a`) |
| `[a-%]]` | `93` (range `a`..`%` is empty, then literal `]`) |
| `[-]`, `[%-]` | `45` |
| `[a-]`, `[-a]` | `45,97` |
| `[--0]` | `45-48` |
| `[+--]` | `43-45` |
| `[a-c-e]` | `45,97-99,101` |
| `[%a]` / `[^%a]` / `[%A]` | `65-90,97-122` / `0-64,91-96,123-255` / same as `[^%a]` |
| `[%d-a]` | `45,48-57,97` — a class is **never** a range endpoint |
| `[a-%d]` | `100` — range `a`..`%` empty, then `d` literal |
| `[%a-z]` | `45,65-90,97-122` |
| `[a-c%d-f]` | `45,48-57,97-99,102` |
| `[%w_]` | `48-57,65-90,95,97-122` |
| `[%z]` / `[^%z]` / `[%Z]` | `0` / `1-255` / `1-255` |
| `[.*+?]` | `42-43,46,63` (no magic inside a set) |
| `[(]` `[)]` `[$]` `[%%]` `[%^]` | `40` `41` `36` `37` `94` |
| `[%b]` `[%f]` `[%1]` | `98` `102` `49` (no special meaning inside a set) |
| `[^^]` | `0-93,95-255` |
| `[a^]` | `94,97` (`^` is negation only immediately after `[`) |
| `[\200-\255]` | `200-255` |
| `[\255-\1]` | *(none)* |

Malformed: `[`, `[^`, `[]`, `[^]`, `[abc`, `[a-`, `[%`, `[%]`, `[a%`, `%f[`,
`%f[%a` all ⇒ `malformed pattern (missing ']')`.

### 1.4 Magic characters and the `find` fast path

`SPECIALS == "$%(*+-.?[^"` (exactly these 10 bytes). Determined empirically:
`string.find` uses a **plain `memchr`/`memcmp` search** whenever the pattern
contains none of them, so:

```
find("a)b", ")")   --> 2   2      (plain search: ')' is not special)
find("a)b", "a)")  --> 1   2
find("a]b", "]")   --> 2   2
find("a)b", ".)")  --> error: invalid pattern capture   ('.' forces real matching)
match("a)b", ")")  --> error: invalid pattern capture   (match has no fast path)
gsub("a)b", ")","-")--> error: invalid pattern capture
```

`)` and `]` are **not** in `SPECIALS`; therefore an unmatched `)` reaches the
matcher only when some other special is present, or when the function is
`match`/`gmatch`/`gsub`.

---

## 2. Quantifiers

`*` `+` `-` `?` apply to the **immediately preceding single-character item**
(a literal byte, `%X` escape/class, `.`, or a `[...]` set) and to nothing else.

| suffix | meaning |
|---|---|
| `*` | 0 or more, **greedy** (longest first, then backtracks shorter) |
| `+` | 1 or more, greedy |
| `-` | 0 or more, **lazy** (shortest first, then extends) |
| `?` | 0 or 1, greedy (tries 1 first) |

```
find("aaa","a*")           --> 1  3
find("baaa","a*")          --> 1  0        (empty match at position 1)
match("<<x>>","<(.*)>")    --> "<x>"
match("<<x>>","<(.-)>")    --> "<x"
match("aaab","(a-)b")      --> "aaa"
match("b","a?")            --> ""
match("aaab","a?a?b")      --> "aab"
match("aaab","(a*)(a*)b")  --> "aaa"  ""
match("aaab","(a-)(a*)b")  --> ""     "aaa"
match("aaa","(a+)(a+)")    --> "aa"   "a"
match("aaa","(a+)(a+)(a+)")--> "a" "a" "a"
```

**A quantifier with nothing to repeat is a literal character**, and a *second*
stacked quantifier is likewise literal:

```
match("aaa","*a")   --> nil        match("*a","*a")  --> "*a"
match("aaa","+a")   --> nil        match("+a","+a")  --> "+a"
match("aaa","?a")   --> nil        match("?a","?a")  --> "?a"
match("aaa","-a")   --> nil        match("-a","-a")  --> "-a"
match("aaa","a**")  --> nil        match("aa*","a**")--> "aa*"
match("aaa","a*+")  --> nil        match("aa+","a*+")--> "aa+"
match("aaa","a??")  --> nil
```

Quantifiers **cannot** be applied to `(...)`, `()`, `%bxy` or `%f[...]`; the
suffix character is a literal:

```
match("abab","(ab)*") --> nil        match("ab*","(ab)*")   --> "ab"
match("aa","()*")     --> nil        match("*","()*")       --> 1
match("(x)(y)","%b()*")--> nil       match("(x)*","%b()*")  --> "(x)*"
match("abc","%f[%a]*")--> nil        match("*abc","%f[%a]*")--> nil
```

Matching is **leftmost-first**, not leftmost-longest: the engine tries start
positions `init, init+1, …, len+1` and returns the first position where the
whole pattern matches (`find("xxabab","ab*") --> 3 4`).

---

## 3. Anchors

* `^` is an anchor **only when it is the first byte of the pattern**. It anchors
  at the *search start* (i.e. at `init`, not necessarily at position 1).
  Everywhere else `^` is a literal byte.
* `$` is an anchor **only when it is the last byte of the pattern** (and is not
  itself escaped). Everywhere else `$` is a literal byte.

```
find("hello","^h")        --> 1  1        find("hello","^e")     --> nil
find("hello","^")         --> 1  0        find("","^")           --> 1  0
find("hello","^^")        --> nil         find("^x","^^")        --> 1  1
find("l^o","l^")          --> 1  2        find("a^b","(a)^(b)")  --> 1 3 "a" "b"
find("hello","^e",2)      --> 2  2        find("xabc","^abc",2)  --> 2  4
find("hello","^",6)       --> 6  5        find("hello","^",7)    --> nil

find("hello","o$")        --> 5  5        find("hello","l$")     --> nil
find("hello","$")         --> 6  5        find("","$")           --> 1  0
find("hello","$$")        --> nil         find("a$","$$")        --> 2  2
find("l$l","l$l")         --> 1  3
match("abc","(c$)")       --> nil     -- '$' before ')' is a literal
match("a$c","(a$c)")      --> "a$c"
match("abc","a*$")        --> ""      -- empty match at position 4
find("abc","$",4)         --> 4  3        find("abc","$",5)      --> nil

Per-function anchor handling:

| function | leading `^` | trailing `$` |
|---|---|---|
| `find` / `match` | anchor: exactly one attempt, at `init` | anchor |
| `gsub` | anchor at position 1; the replacement loop **breaks after the first attempt** | anchor |
| `gmatch` | **NOT** an anchor — `^` is a literal byte | anchor (still end-of-subject) |

```
gsub("aaa","^a","X")      --> "Xaa"  1     gsub("aaa","^a","X",5) --> "Xaa" 1
gsub("aaa","^a*","X")     --> "X"    1     gsub("aaa","^","X")    --> "Xaaa" 1
gsub("","^","X")          --> "X"    1     gsub("bab","^a","X")   --> "bab"  0
gsub("x^ay","^a","Z")     --> "x^ay" 0
gsub("aaa","$","X")       --> "aaaX" 1     gsub("ab","$","X",2)   --> "abX"  1

for w in ("aaa"):gmatch("^a")  do ... end  -- no iterations
for w in ("x^ay"):gmatch("^a") do ... end  -- one iteration, w == "^a"
for w in ("ab"):gmatch("$")    do ... end  -- one iteration, w == ""
```

* `(` … `)` — normal capture, numbered by the order of the **opening** paren.
* `()` — **position capture**: yields the 1-based *integer* index of that point

find ("hello","()l")                --> 3  3  3
match("abc","(c)()")                --> "c"  4
match("abc","(.*)()$")              --> "abc"  4
for p in ("abc"):gmatch("()") do ... end   --> 1, 2, 3, 4
```

### 4.1 Back references `%1` … `%9` in the pattern

`%n` matches the *literal text* previously captured by capture `n`.

```
match("abcabc","(abc)%1")  --> "abc"
match("abcabd","(abc)%1")  --> nil
match("aabc","()(a)%2")    --> 1  "a"
gsub("the the cat sat sat","(%w+) %1","%1") --> "the cat sat"  2
```

Special cases:

* `%n` where capture `n` is a **position** capture never matches (its stored
  length is the sentinel `CAP_POSITION`, which compares as a huge length), but
  it is **not** an error: `match("abc","()%1") --> nil`, `match("abc","(()%2)") --> nil`.
* `%n` where capture `n` is still **open** (unfinished) ⇒
  `invalid capture index %n`: `match("aa","((a)%1)")`, `match("abc","(a%1)")`.
* `%n` with `n` > number of started captures ⇒ `invalid capture index %n`.
* `%0` in a pattern ⇒ `invalid capture index %0`.
* `%1` with no captures at all ⇒ `invalid capture index %1`.

### 4.2 Limits

`LUA_MAXCAPTURES == 32`. The 33rd capture (normal, positional, or nested) ⇒
`too many captures`. Nesting depth is limited only by that count.

```
32 captures -> ok (32 values)          33 captures -> "too many captures"
32 position captures -> ok             33          -> "too many captures"
("("):rep(32).."a"..(")"):rep(32) ok   33 deep      -> "too many captures"
find("abc","z"..("(a)"):rep(33))  --> nil        (lazy: never reached)
```

`find` may therefore return up to `2 + 32 == 34` values.

### 4.3 Unbalanced parentheses

* `(` that is never closed ⇒ `unfinished capture` — but only if the overall
  match succeeds and the captures are pushed (`match("abc","(a$") --> nil`,
  `match("a","(a$") --> error`).
* A `)` with no open capture ⇒ `invalid pattern capture`, raised when the
  matcher *reaches* it (and only when the `find` fast path does not apply).

## 5. `%bxy` — balanced match

`%b` consumes the **next two raw bytes** of the pattern as the opening `x` and
closing `y` delimiters (no `%`-unescaping: `%b%(` uses `'%'` and `'('`).
It requires `s[0] == x`, then scans forward keeping a counter, `+1` on `x`,
`-1` on `y`, returning the position just past the `y` that brings it to 0.
When `x == y` the very next occurrence closes it.

```
match("(a(b)c)","%b()")     --> "(a(b)c)"     find("(a(b)c)","%b()") --> 1 7
match("x(a(b)c)y","%b()")   --> "(a(b)c)"
match("((ab)","%b()")       --> "(ab)"
match("(((","%b()")         --> nil          match(")))","%b()")     --> nil
match("()","%b()")          --> "()"
match("[a[b]c]","%b[]")     --> "[a[b]c]"
match("a<b<c>d>e","%b<>")   --> "<b<c>d>"
match("aXbXc","%bXX")       --> "XbX"        match("XXX","%bXX")     --> "XX"
match("aa","%baa")          --> "aa"         match("a-b-c","%b--")   --> "-b-"
match("\0a\0","%b\0\0")     --> "\0a\0"
match("%(x","%b%(")         --> "%("         -- raw delimiters '%' and '('
gsub("f(a(b))g(c)","%b()","<>") --> "f<>g<>"  2
```

Fewer than two bytes after `%b` ⇒
`malformed pattern (missing arguments to '%b')` (lazy: `find("abc","q%b") --> nil`).

---

## 6. `%f[set]` — frontier

`%f` must be followed by `[`, otherwise ⇒ `missing '[' after '%f' in pattern`
(`%f`, `%fa`, `%f%a`, `%f]` all raise it). `%f[]` / `%f[%a` ⇒
`malformed pattern (missing ']')`.

`%f[set]` matches an **empty string** at position `s` iff
`previous ∉ set` and `current ∈ set`, where

* `previous` is `s[-1]`, or `'\0'` when `s` is the **start of the whole
  subject** (this is the real string start, *not* the `init` offset);
* `current` is `s[0]`, or `'\0'` when `s` is one past the end.

So `%f` can fire at position `len+1`.

```
find("hello","%f[%a]")     --> 1  0
find("hello","%f[%A]")     --> 6  5
find(" ab","%f[%a]")       --> 2  1
find("ab cd","%f[^%a]")    --> 3  2
find("  _x","%f[%w_]")     --> 3  2
find("abc","%f[%z]")       --> 4  3      -- '\0' sentinel at the end
find("x","%f[^\0]")        --> 1  0
find("","%f[%a]")          --> nil       find("","%f[%A]")   --> nil
find("","%f[%z]")          --> nil       find("","%f[^%z]")  --> nil
find("a]b","%f[]]")        --> 2  1
find("abc","^%f[%a]")      --> 1  0      find("abc","^%f[%a]a") --> 1 1
find("  ab","()%f[%a]()")  --> 3 2 3 3

-- the 'previous' byte comes from the real string even before init:
find("ab","%f[%a]",1) --> 1 0     find("ab","%f[%a]",2) --> nil
for _ in ("ab"):gmatch("%f[%a]",2) do end   -- no iterations

gsub("THE (quick) fox","%f[%a]%a+",string.upper) --> "THE (QUICK) FOX"  3
gsub("abc","%f[%a]","|")   --> "|abc"   1
gsub("a b","%f[%a]","|")   --> "|a |b"  2
gsub("a b","%f[%A]","|")   --> "a| b|"  2
gsub("a b c","%f[%s]","|") --> "a| b| c" 2
gsub("a b c","%f[%S]","|") --> "a |b |c" 2
gsub("","%f[%z]","|")      --> ""       0
gsub("x","%f[%z]","|")     --> "x|"     1
```

---

## 7. `string.find (s, pattern [, init [, plain]])`

Returns `start, end` (1-based, inclusive; an empty match yields `end == start-1`)
followed by all captures, or `nil`.

### 7.1 `init`

`init` is converted with `luaL_optinteger` (accepts integer-valued floats and
numeric strings; `1.5` ⇒ `bad argument #3 … (number has no integer
representation)`; `true` ⇒ `… (number expected, got boolean)`).
It is then normalised (`posrelatI`):

```
init > 0            -> init
init == 0           -> 1
init < 0, |init|<=len -> len+init+1
init < 0, |init|>len  -> 1        (also math.mininteger -> 1)
```
Finally `if (normalised > len+1) return nil` — so `init == len+1` is legal
(only the empty match / `$` / `%f` can succeed there) and anything beyond
returns `nil` immediately.

Subject `"hello"`, pattern `"l"`:

| init | result | init | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| −100…−3 | `3 3` | 0…3 | `3 3` |
| −2 | `4 4` | 4 | `4 4` |
| −1 | `nil` | 5,6,7,100 | `nil` |
| `math.mininteger` | `3 3` | `math.maxinteger` | `nil` |

Empty pattern: `find("hello","",i)` returns `i', i'-1`:
`i=−10→1 0`, `−1→5 4`, `0→1 0`, `1→1 0`, `4→4 3`, `5→5 4`, `6→6 5`, `7→nil`.

### 7.2 `plain`

Any **truthy** 4th argument (including `0` and `""`) turns off pattern matching
and does a raw substring search. No captures are ever returned.

```
find("a.c",".",1,true)  --> 2 2      find("a.c",".",1,false) --> 1 1
find("a.c",".",1,0)     --> 2 2      find("a.c",".",1,nil)   --> 1 1
find("a%b","%b",1,true) --> 2 3      find("x(a)y","(a)",1,true) --> 2 4
find("abc","",4,true)   --> 4 3      find("abc","",5,true)   --> nil
find("ab","abc",1,true) --> nil
```

`match`, `gmatch` and `gsub` have no `plain` flag; extra arguments are ignored
(`match("a","a",1,2,3)` is fine).

---

## 8. `string.match (s, pattern [, init])`

Same search as `find`; returns the captures (or the whole match when the
pattern has none), or `nil`. `init` behaves exactly as in `find`.

---

## 9. `string.gmatch (s, pattern [, init])`

Returns a stateful iterator function (`type` is `"function"`); its own
arguments are ignored. A 4th argument to `gmatch` is accepted and ignored.

* `init` uses `posrelatI` then is clamped: `if (init-1 > len) init = len+2`
  effectively, so `init == len+1` still yields the final empty match while
  `init >= len+2` yields nothing.
* **A leading `^` is a plain literal byte** (no anchoring).
* `$` at the end of the pattern still anchors to the end of the subject.
* **`lastmatch` rule:** a candidate match is rejected if its *end* position
  equals the end position of the previous accepted match. This prevents an
  empty match immediately after a non-empty one.

```
("a,b,c"):gmatch("[^,]+")  --> "a" "b" "c"
("a=1, b=2"):gmatch("(%w+)=(%w+)") --> ("a","1") ("b","2")
("abc"):gmatch("")         --> "" "" "" ""            (4 items)
(""):gmatch("")            --> ""                     (1 item)
("abc"):gmatch("x*")       --> "" "" "" ""
("aaa"):gmatch("a*")       --> "aaa"                  (only one!)
("hello"):gmatch("l*")     --> "" "" "ll" ""
("abc"):gmatch("%a*")      --> "abc"
("abc"):gmatch("()a*()")   --> (1,2) (3,3) (4,4)
("aXbXc"):gmatch("X*")     --> "" "X" "X" ""
("XaX"):gmatch("X*")       --> "X" "X"

("hello"):gmatch("%a",3)   --> "l" "l" "o"
("hello"):gmatch("%a",-2)  --> "l" "o"
("hello"):gmatch("%a",0)   --> "h" "e" "l" "l" "o"
("hello"):gmatch("%a",6)   --> (none)
("hello"):gmatch("",5)     --> "" ""
("hello"):gmatch("",6)     --> ""
("hello"):gmatch("",7)     --> (none)
```

Pattern errors are raised on the **first offending iteration**, not when the
iterator is created: `string.gmatch("abc","%")` succeeds; calling the result
raises `malformed pattern (ends with '%')`.

---

## 10. `string.gsub (s, pattern, repl [, n])`

Returns `newstring (string), count (integer)`.

### 10.1 The replacement loop

```
max_n   = n or (#s + 1)          -- default limit is #s+1
lastmatch = nil ; src = start
while count < max_n do
    e = match(src)
    if e and e ~= lastmatch then
        count = count + 1 ; emit replacement ; src = lastmatch = e
    elseif src < end then
        emit s[src] ; src = src + 1
    else break end
    if anchored then break end
end
emit rest of s
```

The `e ~= lastmatch` test is what produces:

```
gsub("hello","l-",".")  --> ".h.e.l.l.o."   6
gsub("hello","l*",".")  --> ".h.e.o."       4
gsub("abc",".-","<>")   --> "<>a<>b<>c<>"   4
gsub("abc","x*","-")    --> "-a-b-c-"       4
gsub("aaa","a*","-")    --> "-"             1
gsub("XaX","X*","-")    --> "-a-"           2
gsub("a,b",",*","-")    --> "-a-b-"         3
gsub("a,,b","([^,]*),?","<%1>") --> "<a><><b>"  3
```

`n` (limit): `nil` ⇒ `#s+1`; `<= 0` ⇒ no replacements, count 0;
`math.mininteger` ⇒ 0; larger than possible is harmless.

```
gsub("aaa","a","X",0)  --> "aaa"  0     gsub("aaa","a","X",2) --> "XXa" 2
gsub("aaa","a","X",4)  --> "XXX"  3     gsub("aaa","a","X",-1)--> "aaa" 0
gsub("","","x")        --> "x"    1     gsub("","a","x")      --> ""    0
gsub("abc","","-")     --> "-a-b-c-" 4  gsub("abc","","-",1)  --> "-abc" 1
gsub("abc","","",2)    --> "abc"  2
```

### 10.2 `repl` is a **string** (or number)

`%0` = whole match, `%1`…`%9` = captures, `%%` = a literal `%`.
`%1` with **no** captures means the whole match. A position capture is
converted with the usual number→string rules.

```
gsub("hello","l","[%0]")        --> "he[l][l]o"   2
gsub("hello","(l)","[%1]")      --> "he[l][l]o"   2
gsub("hello","l","%1")          --> "hello"       2
gsub("ab","(a)(b)","[%0|%1|%2]")--> "[ab|a|b]"    1
gsub("hello","ll","%0%0")       --> "hellllo"     1
gsub("hello","l","[%%]")        --> "he[%][%]o"   2
gsub("50%","%%"," pct")         --> "50 pct"      1
gsub("hello","()l","<%1>")      --> "he<3><4>o"   2
gsub("ab","()","%10")           --> "10a20b30"    3   (%1 then literal '0')
gsub("aaa","a",5)               --> "555"         3
gsub("aaa","a",5.5)             --> "5.55.55.5"   3
```

Errors (raised only when a replacement is actually produced):

* `%` followed by anything that is not a digit and not `%` ⇒
  `invalid use of '%' in replacement string` (also for a trailing `%`).
* `%n` with `n` greater than the number of captures ⇒
  `invalid capture index %n`.

### 10.3 `repl` is a **table**

Indexed (with normal `lua_gettable`, so `__index` **is** honoured) by capture 1,
or by the whole match when there are no captures. Position captures index with
an integer key.

```
gsub("hello world","%w+",{hello="HI",world="EARTH"}) --> "HI EARTH"  2
gsub("hello world","%w+",{hello="HI"})               --> "HI world"  2
gsub("k=v","(%w+)=(%w+)",{k="K"})                    --> "K"         1
gsub("abc","()",{[1]="X",[2]="Y"})                   --> "XaYbc"     4
gsub("abc","%a",{a=1,b=2.5,c=false})                 --> "12.5c"     3
gsub("ab","%a", setmetatable({},{__index=function(_,k) return "<"..k..">" end}))
                                                     --> "<a><b>"    2
```

### 10.4 `repl` is a **function**

Called with all captures (or the whole match if none). Only the **first**
return value is used.

```
gsub("hello","l+",string.upper)                  --> "heLLo"  1
gsub("k=v","(%w+)=(%w+)",function(a,b) return b.."="..a end) --> "v=k" 1
gsub("aba","()a()",function(i,j) return "["..i..","..j.."]" end) --> "[1,2]b[3,4]" 2
gsub("abc","%a",function(c) return c:upper(),"IGNORED" end)  --> "ABC" 3
```

Errors from the function propagate unchanged (`error("boom")` ⇒ `boom`,
prefixed with the position of the `error` call).
`gsub` is **not** yieldable: yielding from the replacement function gives
`attempt to yield across a C-call boundary`.

### 10.5 Replacement value rules (table and function)

* `nil` or `false` ⇒ **keep the original matched text** (still counted).
* string or number ⇒ used (numbers converted with `tostring` semantics:
  `7`→`"7"`, `7.0`→`"7.0"`, `7.5`→`"7.5"`, `-0.0`→`"-0.0"`, `1/0`→`"inf"`,
  `-1/0`→`"-inf"`, `0/0`→`"-nan"`, `1e300`→`"1e+300"`,
  `math.maxinteger`→`"9223372036854775807"`, `2^53`→`"9007199254740992.0"`).
* anything else ⇒ `invalid replacement value (a <type>)` where `<type>` is
  `table`, `boolean`, `thread`, `userdata`, `function`.

---

## 11. Error messages (exact text)

All of these are raised with `luaL_error`, i.e. they carry a
**`chunkname:line: ` prefix taken from the calling Lua frame**. If the C
function is invoked with no Lua frame in between (e.g. `pcall(string.find, …)`)
`luaL_where` yields `""` and the message has **no prefix**.

```
pcall(string.find, "a", "%")             --> "malformed pattern (ends with '%')"
pcall(function() ("a"):find("%") end)    --> "t.lua:1: malformed pattern (ends with '%')"
```

| message | raised by |
|---|---|
| `malformed pattern (ends with '%')` | `%` as the last pattern byte, reached by the matcher |
| `malformed pattern (missing ']')` | `[…` with no closing `]` (also `%f[…`) |
| `malformed pattern (missing arguments to '%b')` | fewer than 2 bytes after `%b` |
| `missing '[' after '%f' in pattern` | `%f` not followed by `[` |
| `unfinished capture` | a `(` still open when captures are pushed |
| `invalid pattern capture` | a `)` with no open capture, reached by the matcher |
| `invalid capture index %N` | `%0`/`%N` out of range or referring to an open capture — **in patterns and in replacement strings alike** (there is no `" in pattern"` / `" in replacement string"` suffix in this build) |
| `too many captures` | 33rd capture started |
| `pattern too complex` | recursion depth exceeded (see below) |
| `invalid use of '%' in replacement string` | `%` + non-digit / trailing `%` in a `gsub` replacement string |
| `invalid replacement value (a table)` / `(a boolean)` / `(a thread)` / `(a userdata)` / `(a function)` | table/function `repl` returned a bad type |

### 11.1 All pattern errors are LAZY

They fire only when the matcher actually reaches the offending item:

```
find("abc","z%")     --> nil     find("abc","%")   --> error
find("abc","z[a")    --> nil     find("abc","[a")  --> error
find("abc","z%b")    --> nil     find("abc","%b")  --> error
find("abc","z%f")    --> nil     find("abc","%f")  --> error
find("abc","z(")     --> nil     find("abc","(")   --> error
find("abc","z%1")    --> nil     find("abc","%1")  --> error
find("abc","a[z]%")  --> nil     find("abc","a[b]%") --> error
find("abc","%b()%")  --> nil     (the %b fails before '%' is reached)
find("abc","z"..("(a)"):rep(33)) --> nil   (no "too many captures")
```

### 11.2 `pattern too complex`

The matcher has a depth budget of **200 nested `match()` invocations**
(`MAXCCALLS`), reset for every start position / every `gsub` iteration.

```
("a-"):rep(199) on "a"  -> ok
("a-"):rep(200) on "a"  -> "pattern too complex"
(".-"):rep(199) on "x"  -> ok
(".-"):rep(200) on "x"  -> "pattern too complex"
("a-"):rep(5000) on ""  -> ok       -- the item never matches, so no recursion
find(("b"):rep(50).."a", ("a-"):rep(199).."a")  --> 51 51   (budget is per attempt)
gsub("aaaa", ("a-"):rep(199).."a", "X")         --> "XXXX" 4
```

Depth grows only when a repetition item *can* match at the current position
(`min_expand`/`max_expand` recurse); a failing single-char item with a `*`/`?`/`-`
suffix is handled by an iterative `goto`, so long patterns of failing items are free.

### 11.3 `bad argument` messages

```
string.find  #1 (string expected, got nil|boolean|no value)
string.find  #2 (string expected, got nil|no value)
string.find  #3 (number expected, got table|boolean|string)
string.find  #3 (number has no integer representation)
string.gsub  #3 (string/function/table expected, got no value|nil|boolean)
string.gsub  #4 (number expected, got string)   /  (number has no integer representation)
string.gmatch #3 (number expected, got string)  /  (number has no integer representation)
```

The **function name** in the message depends on how the C function was reached:

```
pcall(string.find, nil, "x")            -> bad argument #1 to 'string.find' (...)
(function() string.find(nil,"x") end)   -> bad argument #1 to 'find' (...)
local ff=string.find; ff(nil,"x")       -> bad argument #1 to 'ff' (...)
("x"):find(nil)                         -> bad argument #1 to 'find' (...)
```

Numbers are accepted wherever a string is expected (`string.find(121, 2) --> 2 2`).

---

## 12. Embedded NUL bytes

Strings are length-counted; `\0` is an ordinary byte in both subject and
pattern, in plain search, in sets, in `%b` delimiters, and around anchors.

```
s = "a\0b\0c"   -- #s == 5
find(s,"\0")            --> 2 2       find(s,"\0",1,true) --> 2 2
find(s,"b\0c")          --> 3 5
match(s,"a.b")          --> "a\0b"
match(s,"(a)%z(b)")     --> "a" "b"
gsub(s,"\0","X")        --> "aXbXc" 2
gsub("abc","b","x\0y")  --> "ax\0yc" 1
find("a\0b","[\0a]+")   --> 1 2       find("a\0b","[\0-\5]") --> 2 2
match("\0x\0","%b\0\0") --> "\0x\0"
find("a\0","\0$")       --> 2 2       find("\0a","^\0")      --> 1 1
find("a\0b","%f[\0]")   --> 2 1
for c in s:gmatch("[^\0]+") do ... end    --> "a" "b" "c"
```

Round trip over all 256 byte values: `gsub(all,".","")` counts 256,
`gsub(all,"%z","")` counts 1, `gsub(all,"%Z","")` counts 255, and
`gmatch(all,".")` reproduces the string exactly.

---

## 13. Cheat sheet of surprising behaviours

1. `%z` is a real class (byte 0) and `%Z` its complement — unlike stock Lua 5.2–5.4.
2. `)` and `]` are **not** in `SPECIALS`, so `string.find` silently plain-searches
   patterns that `match`/`gsub` would reject with `invalid pattern capture`.
3. `^` is an anchor only as the first pattern byte; `$` only as the last;
   `gmatch` ignores `^` entirely (it becomes a literal).
4. Quantifiers cannot be applied to `(...)`, `()`, `%b`, `%f`; the suffix is a literal.
   A stacked quantifier (`a**`) is `a*` followed by literal `*`.
5. Inside a set, a class (`%a`) can never be a range endpoint — `[a-%d]` is
   `range(a,'%')` (empty) plus literal `d`.
6. Every pattern error is lazy — it only fires if the matcher reaches that item.
7. `invalid capture index %N` has **no** trailing `" in pattern"` /
   `" in replacement string"` qualifier in this build.
8. `%1` in a `gsub` replacement means "whole match" when the pattern has no captures.
9. Back-reference to a **position** capture silently fails to match; back-reference
   to an **open** capture is an error.
10. `gsub`'s default `n` is `#s + 1`, and the `e ~= lastmatch` rule stops an empty
    match from being applied right after a non-empty one at the same end position.
11. `find`/`match`/`gmatch` accept `init == #s + 1`; anything beyond returns
    nothing (for `find` immediately `nil`).
12. `%f`'s "previous character" is the byte before the position in the **whole**
    subject, even when `init` skips past it.
13. Recursion budget is 200 nested `match()` calls ⇒ `pattern too complex`.
14. Error position prefixes appear only when a Lua frame called the C function.

## Most important / surprising findings (ref = Lua 5.5.1)

**Character classes**
1. `%z` is a LIVE class meaning "byte 0" — not the literal letter `z`. `find("z","%z")==nil`, `find("\0","%z")==1,1`. `%Z` is its complement (bytes 1-255, count 255). Differs from stock 5.2-5.4 where `%z` is literal `z`.
2. Exactly 11 class letters: `a c d g l p s u w x z` + uppercase complements. All other 233 `%<byte>` forms are the literal byte. C locale only (`os.setlocale("")` → `"C"`).

**The `find` fast path leaks through**
3. `SPECIALS == "$%(*+-.?[^"` — `)` and `]` are NOT special. So `find("a)b",")") → 2,2` (plain memchr search) while `match("a)b",")")` / `gsub(...)` raise `invalid pattern capture`. `find("a)b",".)")` errors because `.` forces real matching.

**Anchors**
4. `^` anchors only as the *first* pattern byte, and anchors at `init` (`find("xabc","^abc",2) → 2,4`). `find("hello","^^")→nil`, `find("^x","^^")→1,1`.
5. `$` anchors only as the *last* pattern byte: `match("abc","(c$)")→nil` but `match("a$c","(a$c)")→"a$c"`.
6. **`gmatch` ignores `^` entirely** — it becomes a literal: `("aaa"):gmatch("^a")` yields nothing; `("x^ay"):gmatch("^a")` yields `"^a"`. `gsub` does honour it (and breaks after one attempt).

**Quantifiers**
7. `*+-?` with nothing to repeat are literal chars; stacked quantifiers too: `a**` == `a*` then literal `*` (`match("aa*","a**")→"aa*"`).
8. Quantifiers do NOT apply to `(...)`, `()`, `%bxy`, `%f[]`: `match("(x)*","%b()*")→"(x)*"`.

**Sets**
9. A class is never a range endpoint: `[a-%d]` matches only `d` (range `a`..`%` is empty, then literal `d`); `[%d-a]` = digits + `-` + `a`; `[a-c-e]` = `-`,`a-c`,`e`.

**Captures**
10. `LUA_MAXCAPTURES == 32`; 33rd ⇒ `too many captures` (find can return 34 values).
11. Back-reference to a **position** capture silently never matches (`match("abc","()%1")→nil`); to an **open** capture it errors `invalid capture index %1`.
12. `%1` in a gsub replacement string means the whole match when the pattern has no captures.

**Errors**
13. **Every** pattern error is lazy — only fired when the matcher reaches the item: `find("abc","z%")→nil`, `find("abc","%b()%")→nil`, `find("abc","z"..("(a)"):rep(33))→nil`.
14. `invalid capture index %N` has **no** `" in pattern"` / `" in replacement string"` suffix in this build (both contexts share the bare message).
15. Position prefix `chunk:line:` appears only when a Lua frame called the C function; `pcall(string.find,"a","%")` gives the bare message.
16. `bad argument` function name varies by call site: `'string.find'` (direct pcall) vs `'find'` (`string.find(...)`) vs `'ff'` (local alias).
17. Recursion budget = **200** nested `match()` calls → `pattern too complex`: `("a-"):rep(199)` on `"a"` ok, `200` errors. Budget resets per start position / per gsub iteration. `("a-"):rep(5000)` on `""` is free (failing items use an iterative goto).

**gsub / gmatch loop**
18. The `e ~= lastmatch` rule: `gsub("hello","l*",".") → ".h.e.o.", 4` (not `.h.e..o.`), `("aaa"):gmatch("a*")` yields exactly one item `"aaa"`.
19. Default `n` for gsub is `#s+1`. `nil`/`false` from table/function ⇒ keep original text (still counted). Bad types ⇒ `invalid replacement value (a table|boolean|thread|userdata|function)`. gsub table lookups honour `__index`. gsub is not yieldable.
20. `gmatch` takes a 3rd `init` arg (5.4+); a 4th is accepted and ignored; the iterator's own args are ignored.

**Misc**
21. `%f`'s "previous byte" comes from the real string start, even when `init` skips past it (`find("ab","%f[%a]",2)→nil`). `%f` can fire at `len+1` (`find("abc","%f[%z]")→4,3`).
22. `%b` takes the next two **raw** bytes as delimiters (`match("%(x","%b%(")→"%("`); `x==y` allowed (`match("a-b-c","%b--")→"-b-"`).
23. `find`/`match`/`gmatch` accept `init == #s+1`; beyond that `find` returns `nil` immediately. `init` normalisation: `0→1`, `<-len→1`, `mininteger→1`, `maxinteger→nil`.
24. Embedded NULs are fully transparent everywhere (subject, pattern, sets, `%b` delimiters, plain search, error paths).
